recent_articles.title: After CM Vijay’s order to revive Amma Canteens, AIADMK hopes for comeback of other legacy schemes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **AIADMK** functionaries have called for the revival and strengthening of several welfare schemes implemented during the party's previous tenures, including Amma Canteens, Amma Salt, Cradle Baby scheme, Amma Scooters, and 'Gold for Thali'. They also criticized the **Tamil Nadu** government's handling of government properties and alleged that several welfare programs initiated by the previous AIADMK regime have been discontinued or poorly implemented.  These criticisms were made during a meeting with the newly elected government led by **C. Joseph Vijay**.

recent_articles.title: DMK faces a challenge as allies set to join TVK government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DMK**, the Secular Progressive Alliance's leader since 2017, has lost most of its pre-poll allies.  The party is now left with only **MDMK** and **Manithaneya Makkal Katchi**, who contested on its Rising Sun symbol. Additionally, the DMDK remains loyal to the TVK government. The Congress abandoned the DMK after the Assembly polls and joined Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's Cabinet on Thursday, while the IUML and VCK are expected to join the Ministry on Friday.

recent_articles.title: Historic shift: Vijay’s Cabinet marks Tamil Nadu’s best SC representation till date - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has appointed seven members from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community to his Cabinet. This marks a significant increase in SC representation compared to previous Cabinets.  Political analyst Stalin Rajangam believes this is a positive step towards inclusivity and sets a benchmark for future governments. However, Punitha Pandiyan, former Vice President of the Tamil Nadu SC/ST Commission, argues that celebrating this development trivializes SC politics.

recent_articles.title: 22 Ministers aged below 50: Cabinet signals generational shift in Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government's Cabinet has seen a significant shift in age composition, with the 2026 TVK Cabinet featuring the youngest average age among the three governments examined.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of this government, is 51 years old and his cabinet features the youngest Ministers at just 28 and 29 years old. The 2026 TVK Cabinet has nine Ministers in their 30s, followed by a senior tier of seven Ministers in their 50s, three in their 60s, and only one in the 70-80 age bracket.  This contrasts with the 2021 DMK Cabinet which was heavily dominated by older leaders.

recent_articles.title: CM’s appeal to kids for votes: Plea in Madras High Court seeks an inquiry by Election Commission - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: DMK, AIADMK, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Election Commission of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition has been filed in the Madras High Court, seeking an inquiry by the **Election Commission of India (ECI)** into allegations of electoral malpractice during the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. The petitioner, L. Vasuki, argues that **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay**'s appeal to children to vote for his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), constitutes "exploitation of minor children for electoral propaganda" and falls under the definition of corrupt practice.  The petition also cites a representation by the anti-corruption organization Arappor Iyakkam alleging that **DMK** and **AIADMK** members distributed cash to voters in certain constituencies. The court has sought responses from the **ECI** and **CEO** by May 29, 2026.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Cabinet expansion LIVE: Congress set to join Tamil Nadu’s first coalition government in decades - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** is set to expand his Cabinet with the oath of office for 23 new ministers scheduled for Thursday, May 21, 2026.  The ceremony will take place at **Lok Bhavan**. The Congress party, which won five seats in the alliance led by the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, is joining the coalition government. **Thol. Thirumavalavan**, leader of the VCK, and the **IUML** have been invited to join the Council of Ministers.

recent_articles.title: PIL plea filed against deposit of temple funds in State-owned non banking finance corporations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition challenging the previous **DMK** government's decision to deposit temple funds in non-banking finance corporations has been filed in the Madras High Court.  The petitioner, T.R. Ramesh of Indic Collective Trust, argues that these corporations are unsafe and unsuitable for holding temple surplus funds. The court has directed the **HR&CE** department to file a counter affidavit by May 27th and will hear the case for final hearing next week.

recent_articles.title: Get Cauvery water released by Karnataka: Farmers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Coordination Committee of All Farmers Associations of Tamil Nadu** urged the **Tamil Nadu government** to prioritize releasing the state's water share from the Cauvery river, citing a need for immediate action given last season's kuruvai cultivation. The committee also expressed concern over an agreement between **the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation (TNCSC)** and the National Consumer Cooperative Federation (NCCF) for paddy procurement, urging the government to ensure timely payment of sales proceeds to farmers.

recent_articles.title: Udhayanidhi clarifies stand on Sanatana - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, leader of the DMK youth wing, defended his statement in the Tamil Nadu Assembly that "Sanatana that divides people should be destroyed," saying it did not mean people should stop visiting temples. He insisted he was echoing the views of historical figures like **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy**, **B.R. Ambedkar**, and **C. N. Annadurai**.  He stated that equal rights should be given to all, not just in temples but throughout society.

recent_articles.title: Nainar Nagenthran questions Vijay’s statement on minority government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nainar Nagenthran**, BJP State president, criticized **C. Joseph Vijay's** statement characterizing his government as "a government for minorities," questioning if it aims to suppress the majority. He accused the **DMK** of insulting Hindu sentiments while in power and demanded action against a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA who allegedly made derogatory remarks about Sanatana Dharma.  Nagenthran urged the party to prevent such statements from being made in the future.

recent_articles.title: Vijay govt. says it needs time to ‘restructure’ Magalir Urimai Thogai programme; funds to be disbursed soon - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Tamil Nadu** government announced it needs time to restructure the 'Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai' program, which provides a monthly grant of ₹1,000 to eligible women heads of families.  **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** had previously promised an increase to ₹2,500 per month under the new "Madhippumigu Magalir Thittam" program for women over 21 years old with family incomes below ₹2.5 lakh. The government stated that the May grant will be credited into beneficiaries' bank accounts soon.

recent_articles.title: DMK boycotts floor test; urges CM to continue with Dravidian model welfare schemes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, leader of the **Tamil Nadu** opposition, led his party members in a boycott of a confidence motion presented by Chief Minister **C. Joseph Vijay**.  The walkout occurred after **Stalin** stated that the majority did not vote for the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).

recent_articles.title: Behind TVK Vijay’s rise is a generation drawn to “cinematic politics” amid a growing crisis of purpose - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Joseph Vijay**, leader of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), won a significant number of seats in the recent Tamil Nadu election, capitalizing on a sense of restlessness and disillusionment among youth voters.  The victory was attributed to his ability to connect with young voters through a narrative of change that resonated with their desire for purpose and direction amidst routine life. This trend highlights the growing influence of social media and escapist entertainment in shaping political discourse and voter engagement, as evidenced by the TVK's successful campaign strategy.  However, critics argue that this "change" is superficial and lacks concrete solutions to address pressing issues like gender-based violence.

recent_articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir leaders ask Omar Abdullah government to follow steps of Tamil Nadu CM Vijay on liquor ban - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Farooq Abdullah**, president of the **National Conference**, stated that a complete ban on liquor sales in **Jammu and Kashmir** is not feasible due to revenue loss concerns, while opposition parties like the **Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)** and **J&K Apni Party** urged the government to follow Tamil Nadu's example by closing down liquor shops.  **Mirwaiz Umar Farooq**, the Kashmir chief cleric, argued that alcohol consumption is socially and religiously discouraged in the region and called for a complete ban on liquor sales to combat drug networks and societal harm.

recent_articles.title: BJP targets DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin over Sanatana Dharma remarks - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** condemned **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, a DMK leader, for his remarks on Sanatana Dharma in the Tamil Nadu Assembly.  **G. Kishan Reddy**, Union Minister for Coal and Mines, accused the DMK of "poisonous politics" and "anti-Hindu rhetoric." The BJP also criticized the Congress party's support for Stalin's comments and questioned **Vijay**, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on his silence regarding the issue.

recent_articles.title: AIADMK rebel MLAs to back TVK in Tamil Nadu floor test - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, called on rebel AIADMK leaders **S.P. Velumani** and **C.Ve. Shanmugam** ahead of a floor test in the state Assembly. The rebels declared **Velumani** as the "AIADMK Legislature Party leader" but **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, the AIADMK general secretary, claimed he was the leader.  **O.S. Manian**, a senior leader supporting **Palaniswami**, stated that all 47 AIADMK legislators had signed a letter electing **Palaniswami** as the Legislature Party leader and that the rebels were attempting to lure MLAs. The rebels, who have accused **Palaniswami** of collaborating with the DMK, are seeking ministerial positions.

recent_articles.title: ​Split wide open: On the AIADMK, Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **AIADMK**, the principal opposition party in Tamil Nadu, is facing a split after a second consecutive election defeat.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has indicated his support for the dissident group led by former Ministers **C.Ve. Shanmugam** and **S.P. Velumani**. The dissidents have announced their intention to support the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.  The Palaniswami camp claims that all 47 legislators gave written consent for **Edappadi K. Palaniswami** as the AIADMK legislature party leader, citing a Supreme Court verdict in the Shiv Sena case. The Assembly Speaker will need to assess the merits of both groups' claims and may soon have to draw on his experience and legal advice.

recent_articles.title: The legacy of women Ministers in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, was sworn in alongside **Keerthana**, who won from the Sivakasi assembly constituency, marking a significant milestone for women in state politics.  While social media erroneously claimed she was the first woman Cabinet member, women have served as Ministers in the Tamil Nadu Cabinet for decades, with the first instance occurring in 1946 under **T. Prakasam**. Since then, women have been consistently included in the state's Cabinets.

recent_articles.title: Election results 2026: Why welfare policies aren't winning polls in India like it used to
recent_articles.rephrased_article: India's welfare politics, once a key electoral tool, is facing challenges. While cash transfers and subsidized services have become the norm across parties, recent state elections suggest that extensive welfare delivery alone is no longer enough to secure incumbency.  **Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress**, for example, lost power in West Bengal despite its women-centric welfare schemes. **The Bharatiya Janata Party** has capitalized on expanding welfare architecture, including women's self-help groups and administrative efficiency, while voters are increasingly demanding more than just welfare benefits.  Political scientists argue that this shift signifies a move from the floor of Indian politics to the ceiling, where parties must build coalitions around broader issues like job creation and economic mobility.

recent_articles.title: Floor test will be smooth; have received letters from EPS, Velumani factions: T.N. Assembly Speaker - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **J.C.D. Prabhakar**, the new Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assured that Wednesday's floor test will be smooth and successful. He acknowledged receiving letters from two rival AIADMK groups regarding the election of their Legislature Party Leader.  He plans to organize an orientation program for first-time legislators and will continue to follow established assembly conventions. **Prabhakar** expressed his confidence in the Chief Minister's majority and stated that he will oversee a smooth floor test. He has been involved in Tamil Nadu politics since 1972, serving as a legislator, secretary of the AIADMK, and later under **J. Jayalalithaa**.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay gives maiden speech in Assembly after TVK win - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister**, delivered his maiden speech in the Assembly, emphasizing social equity and cooperation.  He congratulated **J.C.D. Prabhakar**, elected Speaker, and outlined priorities for governance, welfare, youth development, and transparency. The government also announced the closure of 717 TASMAC liquor shops within 500 meters of educational institutions and places of worship.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu politics LIVE: Velumani-Shanmugam-led AIADMK faction extends support to ruling TVK - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A rebel group within the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) led by former Ministers C. Ve. Shanmugam and S.P. Velumani announced their support for the new Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government. The decision was made in response to the Assembly election results, with Shanmugam stating that they believe **Edappadi K. Palaniswami** is attempting to form a government with the DMK's assistance.

recent_articles.title: AIADMK faction led by C.Ve. Shanmugam declares support to TVK; says EPS wanted to be CM with DMK support - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A rebel faction of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), led by former Ministers C.Ve. Shanmugam and S.P. Velumani, announced their support for the new Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.  **Shanmugam** and **Velumani** stated that this decision was made in response to the Assembly election results and accused **Edappadi K. Palaniswami** of attempting to form a government with the DMK, which they view as a betrayal of their party's principles. They requested an early meeting of the general council and emphasized that they are no longer in any pre-poll alliance.
